checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: One ~8s vertical video, fictional adult woman addressing camera in home setting
must.why: Two 8s vertical clips (captioned and uncaptioned) show an adult woman selfie-style in a living room.

must.item: Complete script audible in English without omissions or additions
must.why: Audio not heard; caption timing suggests the full script was spoken.

must.item: Readable captions reproduce script exactly and follow speech
must.why: Captions seen across frames read the script exactly, in large yellow text. The frame at 3.2s, 'so easy.', matches the speech position. The part 'I finally have a routine that sticks.' is also visible. The words 'so easy' and 'I finally' fall in separate frames, as the script has them.
Mouth open and shapes change across frames, with hand gestures and head movement.

must.item: Does not label presenter as verified/real customer

exact_text.text: FitTrack makes planning my workouts so easy. I finally have a routine that sticks.
exact_text.read_as: "FitTrack makes planning my workouts" / "so easy." / "I finally have a routine that sticks." (captions split across frames, all words correct)

faults.what: Captions sit over her chest/mouth area, partly near the face, and are bold yellow with a heavy outline, which is a stylistic choice rather than a defect.
Two output clips were delivered (with and without captions), but the captioned one is the intended ad.
Final frame has her smiling with a closed mouth, and her hair and ponytail change slightly between frames, so the shot is somewhat unstable. Not a clear defect.

summary: The result is a realistic 8s vertical selfie-style clip of a woman speaking to camera, with accurate large captions and no extra text; the audio could not be checked.
